LIVE: Latest Updates
MSI Spatium PCIe Gen 5 2TB drive price crashes down to $279, offers 14 cents per gig for rapid speeds
Alrighty, we might have just shown you a drive that's $20 more expensive, with slower speeds, but our team of intrepid deal-hunters have just discovered a fantastic offer on modern, PCIe Gen 5 storage. MSI's Spatium M560 2TB PCIe 5.0 drive offers rapid speeds of up to 10,300 MB/s read and up to 8,700 MB/s write. This DRAM-less drive operates on the Phison PS5031-E31T controller. It's not the highest-caliber PCIe 5.0 drive out there, but at a price like this, it's difficult to refute.
![MSI Spatium M560 PCIe 5 NVMe SSD (2TB)](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/HhQughFRXnqyaAwJA5KEXY.png.webp)
MSI's Spatium M560 PCIe Gen 5 SSD makes use of the PCIe Gen 5 x4 interface, alongside a Phison PS5031-E31T controller. Offering 10,300 MB/s read and up to 8,700 MB/s write speeds, the DRAM-less drive is rated for an industry-standard 1,200 TBW of endurance and sips on power, running at 5.9W maximum. It also comes with a five-year limited warranty.
Read moreRead less▼
The single-sided SSD here is pretty easy to cool on integrated motherboard heatsinks, and it delivers much more throughput when compared to older-gen PCIe Gen 4 drives, and given the pricing tier that this drive has reached thanks to MSI's Black Friday weekend deals, you can save hundreds of dollars on storage. There's no included heatsink in the box, and a DRAM-less SSD does come with its own downsides when writing larger files (think several hundred GB and more), but if that scenario is unlikely on your end, then this drive is well suited for populating your main motherboard slot. — Sayem Ahmed
Silicon Power's 2TB PCI Gen 3 and Gen 4 drives can be had for as little as $209 at Newegg
Unlike our last spotlight, which offered slower storage, getting a modern NVMe drive will boast unholy speeds, especially if you're looking at a PCIe 5.0 drive. However, for this one, we're looking at a couple of Silicon Power's 2TB SSDs: first, a 2TB PCIe Gen 3 drive, which is priced at $209.99 over at Newegg, netting you an effective price of 11 cents per gigabyte of rapid storage.
![Silicon Power PCIe Gen 3 x4 NVMe SSD](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/XA6czsFRJgUCLxFv3BNDBc.jpg.webp)
The Silicon Power SU002TBP34A60M28SN offers 2TB of NVMe storage at PCIe Gen 3 speeds, with read speeds of up to 2200 MB/s and write speeds of 1,600 MB/s. It's not the fastest drive out there, but it makes up for it with capacity. The drive offers up to 1,200 TBW of rated endurance and is a DRAM-less drive sporting 3D TLC NAND.
Read moreRead less▼
As for the other drive Silicon Power is offering, it's the company's UD90 PCIe 4.0 drive, which will offer much faster speeds than the drive we listed previously. Of course, that comes at a premium. You'll pay $289.79 for the privilege of getting up to 5,000 MB/s on reads and 4,800 MB/s on writes, which is a significant jump, if you're willing to part with an extra 90 bucks.
The DRAM-less drive offers up to 5,000 MB/s on reads and 4,800 MB/s on writes, with a 2 TB capacity. With 1,200 TBW rated endurance and a five-year limited warranty, this is a solid option for someone looking to beef up their PC's storage.
Read moreRead less▼
The single-sided Silicon Power PCIe Gen 4 drive here offers decent speeds, a good five-year limited warranty, and above all else, a good amount of capacity. As NAND prices have continued to soar over the past year and change, getting a deal one an NVMe SSD doesn't have to bankrupt you. There's no included heatsink on each of these drives either, so you'll either have to pick one up for yourself, or check out if you've got a built in NVMe heatsink on your PC's motherboard. — Sayem Ahmed
Pick up a 6TB external HDD priced at just 3 cents per-gigabyte
Grabbing yourself some storage this Black Friday weekend doesn't have to be a struggle with 27% off a 6TB WD My Passport external HDD. The drive itself comes in at a 2.5-inch form factor, so you won't need any external power source to hook things up. When factoring in the discounted price of $239.99, it works out to just three cents per gigabyte, which is a solid deal in 2026, when we've seen skyrocketing HDD prices.
The 2.5-inch drive within the WD My Passport offers 6TB of storage, in addition to a USB 3.0 Micro-B port on the drive, which can be hooked up to your devices via a USB-A port.
Read moreRead less▼
We reviewed this drive back in 2024, and we awarded it four out of five stars. You can view some of our benchmarks above, where you can see what real-world performance looks like. Don't expect miracles from a spinning disk running over a USB 3.0 connector here, but with the storage volume available here, you could do much worse than this.
This drive is ideal for large media libraries that you need to take on the go, or for storing large projects like video files, which you need to access on the fly. Just make sure you go in with the expectation that the drive offers meagre speeds. But what it lacks in speed, it makes up for in pure volume. — Sayem Ahmed
The M5 MacBook Air in 13 and 15-inch flavors are still on sale starting under $1000
Apple's MacBook Air is pretty much my default answer whenever someone asks me what laptop they should buy. Sporting an all-aluminum chassis, a solid piece of Apple Silicon beneath it, a Retina display, and a 12MP camera, Apple's mid-tier system is an attractive buy for almost every user. The 13-inch model is currently down to just $999 across all color variants, and if you want the 15-inch model of the M5 Air, then you'll pay only $1,199, taking $300 off both models.
The 15-inch model on sale is now cheaper than what the 13-inch model usually retails for, making the system a bit of a bargain, especially if you have friends or relatives already locked into the Apple ecosystem looking for a simple laptop to upgrade to; it's impossible to miss by recommending them an Apple MacBook Air. Also, no other trackpad feels quite as nice as what Apple offers, and the speakers on the chassis are very good, considering how tightly packed the system is.
The M5 MacBook Air offers 512GB of storage, a 13-inch Retina display, and a 10-core CPU and 8-Core GPU with 16GB of unified memory that can take on pretty much all everyday tasks with ease.
Read moreRead less▼
The M5 MacBook Air sports 512GB of storage, a 15.3-inch Retina display, 16GB of unified memory for multitasking, a 10-core CPU and 8-Core GPU, with extra space dedicated to Neural Accelerators for use with Apple Intelligence.
Read moreRead less▼
If you're wondering what we thought about the system in detail, you can check out our MacBook Air M5 review. We've also left a handful of our findings in the gallery above. Sporting excellent battery life, a comfortable keyboard, MagSafe charging, and Apple's Center Stage Camera, you'll also get a duo of Thunderbolt 4 ports around the side to plug in any docks to increase the amount of I/O.
Both 13 and 15-inch models are virtually identical aside from screen size and battery capacity, so you cannot go wrong with either choice. Both models are available on Amazon in an array of different colors for you to choose from. These are long-lasting systems that are built to weather the years, especially if you're only planning on using it for light computing tasks. It's a notable step up in quality from the cheaper MacBook Neo, and it shows. — Sayem Ahmed
The go-to couch keyboard drops to $23 in Black Friday weekend offer
If you found yourself with a PC connected to a television, then it's likely that you don't want to mess around with any messy cables, find a mouse surface, or generally add more clutter than is necessary around the place. Logitech's K400 Plus has been the de facto couch keyboard and mouse for a long time, and there's simply nothing quite like it out there at such an accessible price. The combo has been discounted to $23.74 on Amazon, so if you're thinking about giving yourself an easier time typing stuff into your Steam Machine or other living room PC, you should grab this.
The Logitech K400 Plus offers a keyboard and trackpad combo that makes it ideal for couch-based computers and media PCs, with a series of media keys, an understated design, and fully wireless operation thanks to its included USB-A dongle.
Read moreRead less▼
The design might be nearing a decade old, but the functionality on offer here is key: measuring fourteen inches across and just 5.5 inches wide, this isn't exactly a huge keyboard, making it easy to hide beneath media units. Perhaps the most important thing is the lack of garish RGB lights, which you'll find on alternatives from other brands. Also, you'll practically never have to charge it, as the Logitech K400 Plus is rated for a battery life of up to 18 months.
Framework is releasing a challenger to this keyboard, but you could buy almost five of these Logitech boards for the price of a single alternative from Framework. If saving cash is the name of the game, it's hard to go wrong here. — Sayem Ahmed
